title: Split into a module
description:
This program converts temperatures, but everything is in `main.c`. Split it up:

- `convert.h`: an include guard named `CONVERT_H`, and the prototypes of the three conversion functions.
- `convert.c`: includes `"convert.h"` and defines the functions, with the helper `round1` made `static` so only `convert.c` can see it.
- `main.c`: includes `"convert.h"` and keeps only `main`.

The output must stay exactly the same. For every line `20 C` (Celsius), `68 F` (Fahrenheit) or `293.15 K` (Kelvin) it prints the temperature in all three, rounded to one decimal.
hints: `main.c` used `round1` itself in its `printf`. Once `round1` is private to `convert.c`, `main.c` must do its own rounding, for example `round(c * 10.0) / 10.0`, which needs `math.h`.
rules: Give convert.h an include guard named CONVERT_H.

examples.name: an unknown unit
examples.expected:
Unknown unit: X
37.0 C = 98.6 F = 310.2 K
